title: Describing Things
description: The everyday describing words, mostly in pairs: big and small, cheap and expensive, near and far. They go after the noun: rumah besar, a big house.

items.pitfallNote: Describing words go after the noun: rumah besar (a big house), not besar rumah.

items.registerNotes: Waktu kecil means as a child, and kamar kecil (little room) is the polite word for the toilet.
At a market, Mahal sekali (very expensive) or Terlalu mahal (too expensive), said with a smile, opens the bargaining.

items.pitfallNote: Murah is a compliment: good value. Cheap and nasty is murahan.
Before a verb, baru means just: Saya baru datang (I've just arrived). Before a number it means only so far: baru dua hari (only two days).
Lama is old as in not new or former (rumah lama, my old house) and a long time (Sudah lama di sini?). Old in age, for people, is tua.
Bagus is good for things, places and work: Bagus sekali. For people and health, use baik: Kabar baik.

items.registerNotes: Blunt. To be kind, say kurang bagus (not so good).

items.pitfallNote: Hot in temperature: the weather, food, a drink. Chilli-hot is pedas, and warm is hangat: teh hangat.

items.registerNotes: Ask for air dingin if you want your drinking water chilled rather than at room temperature.

items.pitfallNote: Unlike most describing words, banyak goes before the noun: banyak orang (lots of people). Terima kasih banyak is thank you very much.

items.registerNotes: The modest, usual answer to Bisa bahasa Indonesia? (Can you speak Indonesian?) is Sedikit-sedikit (just a little).
Cepat sembuh, ya means get well soon. To a driver going too fast: Jangan cepat-cepat, Pak.
For slow service, internet or traffic. To ask someone to slow down or speak slowly, people say pelan-pelan instead.
items.pitfallNote: Late is terlambat, from the same word; casually, telat.

items.registerNotes: The everyday word for slow and gentle, usually doubled: Pelan-pelan, Pak (slowly, please). Bisa bicara pelan-pelan? asks someone to speak slowly.
items.pitfallNote: Pelan also means quiet: suaranya pelan (his voice is soft).

items.registerNotes: Jauh dari sini? (Is it far from here?) and Masih jauh? (Is it much further?) are the questions to ask on the way.
Dekat sini means near here: Ada ATM dekat sini? Of people, dekat means close: kami dekat (we're close).
Air bersih is clean water for washing, not necessarily for drinking.
